Cori: Heads-up — running a planned rehearsal tomorrow 2026-05-02 03:00 UTC. Goal: validate preemptive fallback + new SLO scheduling window logic on west-1 pools. Estimated impact: short p99 latency blips for a subset of routes (5-15%), lasting ~10m per subpool.

Raj: Which pools exactly? any dedicated customers affected?

Cori: Only west-1 gpu-pool-a and gpu-pool-b (a small reserved set). Dedicated customers with pinned capacity will be routed to fallback model variant; no token loss. We're testing route-level SLO window expansion that allows 15s extra tail tolerance before fallback.

Miguel: Any changes we need to make to alerting/ops runbooks?

Cori: Please reduce SLO burn rate alert sensitivity for the window: change burn rate alert -> 3x for 20m to 4x for 30m. Patch runbook: /runbooks/fallback-rehearsal (link), and set deploy freeze for affected services from 02:30-04:00 UTC.

Olivia: I'll coordinate with TurboBatch and KV team to warm up prefixes before 02:45. Will post warmup confirmation.

Jen: Oncall — watch for customer error rate >0.1% and rollback plan (route fallback off) is in the runbook. @sre-bot will post automated status updates.

sre-bot: Scheduled maintenance posted: id=maint-20260502-west1-fallback, window=03:00-03:30 UTC, tags=[slo-experiment, fallback-rehearsal]. I'll ping channel at start/halfway/end.

Cori: Thanks all. TL;DR — rehearsal 03:00 UTC, expect small p99 blips, avoid deploys, runbook + alerts updated. Ping me if you see anything unexpected. :wave:
